newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo to file combined Retrovir/Epivir.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo to file combined Retrovir/Epivir.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Friday that it planned to seek regulatory approval for a tablet combining two of its leading HIV and AIDS drugs, Epivir and Retrovir.

In its research and development update, the company said the two drugs had "spearheaded a revolution in the treatment of HIV and provided the basis of renewed optimism that the use of drugs can at least keep the disease at bay."
Retrovir and Epivir are the cornerstone of new cocktails of drugs which have led to a breakthrough in treatment for the condition.
Glaxo also gave details of two further HIV/AIDS drugs and said it planned to seek regulatory approval for both in 1998.

It said clinical trials of a new generation of nucleoside analogue, the same class of drug as Retrovir/AZT, showed that when used on its own it reduced levels of the virus in the blood as successfully as protease inhibitors, the third element in the cocktail of new drugs which have provided dramatic progress in treating the condition.

Trials of a new protease inhibitor, a class of drugs which inhibit a key part of the virus's ability to reproduce itself, demonstrated "impressive potency and a good cross resistance and side-effect profile," Glaxo Wellcome said.
